## Source-context gate (#2993)

- Commons' dated upload record (29 March 2010, 02:24 UTC) identifies the SVG as a Babylonian numeral chart based on the earlier raster, made in Inkscape. The file history has only this 2010 upload and two 2021 edits (compression, then reversion). This is evidence of the period file, not of which article LP2's author consulted.
- Inspection of the preserved 220,819-byte SVG finds exactly 59 text spans, the labels 1 through 59 in ascending order. No additional caption, metadata element or textual instruction is present; the sole XML comment identifies Inkscape. Thus no second operand, reading direction or cipher rule is embedded in the source's textual layer.
- [MacTutor, Babylonian numerals](https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/HistTopics/Babylonian_numerals/) (article dated December 2000) independently explains ordinary left-to-right positional base 60, spacing within versus between digit groups, and ambiguous absolute place values in historical notation. It supports the already-established 17,13 → 1033 and 55,1 → 3301 reading given integer context. It is not evidence that this article or its artwork was used by LP2. Neither the upload description nor the SVG singles out fractional positioning, addition, or a recipient cipher operation.
- Current Commons file usage includes the English Wikipedia Babylonian cuneiform numerals, Sexagesimal and 60 articles. Their 2010–2014 article revisions and the original Commons description revision could not be retrieved through the public revision-history/API queries; dated search results did not supply a verified contemporary article containing this specific chart. The [raster file's current description](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Babylonian_numerals.jpg) contains an unrelated decimal illustration with unverified edit date, so it cannot be promoted to a period instruction. Exact original page HTML and date of first article embedding remain unavailable.

**Disposition:** bounded negative on the authenticated file/upload context; no independently selected new operation. Do not repeat base-60 arithmetic or the SVG geometric match. This does not rule out a different historic image source or a now-missing article context. #2994 separately owns historical raster comparison.
